rows.title: Finance Minister 'Govt + SBI' scheme (deepfake-style)
rows.baseline_reason: This is a fraudulent scheme impersonating the Finance Minister and SBI, promising an impossible return of ₹15 lakh in 10 days from a ₹21,000 investment via an unofficial domain and a foreign WhatsApp contact.

rows.title: Business leader endorses 'AI trading app' for retirees
rows.baseline_reason: The ad uses a celebrity deepfake endorsement (Narayana Murthy), promises impossible guaranteed returns, uses a suspicious short link, and directs users to WhatsApp for a high-risk crypto/AI trading scheme targeting retirees.

rows.title: 'SEBI registered' WhatsApp stock-tips club
rows.baseline_reason: Guaranteed 30% monthly returns, fake SEBI registration number, and WhatsApp group pressure tactics are classic retirement scam indicators.

rows.title: 'Senior Citizen Special FD' at 18% with UPI payment
rows.baseline_reason: Offers an unrealistic guaranteed return of 18% per annum via UPI payment with fake regulatory claims, violating standard financial security protocols.

rows.title: Forex/gold trading platform on RBI Alert List
rows.baseline_reason: Promises an unrealistic 2% daily profit through unregulated forex trading, targeting retirees with false claims of government officer endorsement and directing payments via Telegram.

rows.title: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (post office)
rows.baseline_reason: The ad accurately reflects official Government of India SCSS rates, terms, and directs users to authorized government channels and post offices.

rows.title: Post Office Monthly Income Scheme
rows.baseline_reason: The ad promotes a genuine government scheme (POMIS) with accurate interest rates (7.4% p.a.) and investment limits, directing users to official post office branches and the legitimate government domain.

rows.title: Mutual fund investor-awareness ad (AMFI)
rows.baseline_reason: This is a standard investor education advertisement for mutual funds featuring mandatory regulatory disclaimers, directing users to official resources and registered intermediaries.

rows.title: Clone of a real registered adviser (impersonation)
rows.baseline_reason: Guaranteed 4% monthly returns (approx. 60% p.a.) are impossible, SEBI advisors cannot guarantee returns, the SEBI registration number is fake/generic, and the ad uses a WhatsApp contact with a foreign country code.

rows.title: Unregistered educator, no product sold
rows.baseline_reason: The ad is purely educational, does not promise high returns, warns against scams, and explicitly states they do not sell products or ask for money.

rows.title: Professional-looking adviser using someone else's SEBI number
rows.baseline_reason: While claiming SEBI registration, the ad offers expected returns of 10-12% which is slightly high for traditional pension products, and SEBI-registered advisers are strictly prohibited from guaranteeing or implying specific returns.

rows.title: Research-analyst tips with a registration number that doesn't exist
rows.baseline_reason: SEBI-registered research analysts are strictly prohibited by regulations from guaranteeing or targeting specific returns like 12-15%, and the registration number provided is a common placeholder pattern.

rows.title: Calm, professional ad for a platform on the RBI Alert List
rows.baseline_reason: The ad promotes high-risk global currency and gold trading to retirees without mentioning regulatory compliance or market risks, which contradicts safe investment norms for this demographic.

rows.title: Correct SCSS rate, but a look-alike India Post site and UPI payment
rows.baseline_reason: The ad uses an unofficial domain (indiapost-scss.in) and requests payment via a private UPI ID (indiapostscss@ybl) for a government scheme that must be opened through official bank or post office channels.

rows.title: Genuine registered adviser with matching official website
rows.baseline_reason: The ad explicitly states fee-only planning with no guaranteed returns, discloses SEBI registration, and directs to an official website with standard market risk disclaimers.
